failure_summary.description: Searches or filters were left unsaved, or cached retrieval was nested instead of assigned before use.
Follow-up constraints were handled with an inappropriate cached base or by repeating searches instead of updating cached results.
A hotel traveler count was inferred from a generic description of a family with kids.
A restaurant request with sufficient location information was skipped while seeking missing hotel dates.

patch.reasoning: The existing skill already directly covers result assignment and saving, incremental cache updates, and completing available domains when another domain lacks required inputs, so repeating those rules would not patch a gap. Clarify that a generic family description does not establish a hotel headcount, addressing the one concrete ambiguity that led to an unsupported optional parameter.

edits.target: For a hotel search, map any explicitly stated party size to `num_people` (for example, “solo” means `num_people=1`); apply a newly supplied count with a same-domain filter on a suitable cached hotel result when needed. Do not infer unspoken counts or pass traveler counts to flight tools.
edits.content: For a hotel search, map an explicitly stated headcount or party size with a clearly specified number to `num_people` (for example, “solo” means `num_people=1`). Generic descriptions such as “a family” or “a family with kids” do not specify a traveler count; leave `num_people` unset unless the user provides one. Apply a newly supplied count with a same-domain filter on a suitable cached hotel result when needed. Do not infer unspoken counts or pass traveler counts to flight tools.
